source_ref: Christopher M, Ferry M, Simmons A, Vasquez A, Reynolds B, Grupe D (2024) Psychometric properties of the Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire-short form among law enforcement officers. Aggressive Behavior 50(2):e22145, doi:10.1002/ab.22145 (author manuscript PMC11559212); OSF deposit https://osf.io/bskn9/ -- 'Data Dictionary_RMH.xlsx' (https://osf.io/download/2ch6y/, sha256 995ff7604c5a95e1da275668d40733987f832cec817bb16707b99317b9755d82) measure 'scssf' rows q1..q12 and 'BPAQ CFA dataset final_RMH.csv' (https://osf.io/download/m83xq/, sha256 2138710aaa0bb5f3360e0d9cbb47a4e4ae94d50e0fc8364d43d6dba16ada642e); processing script data/BPAQ_Christopher_2024.R; anchors and instructions from Neff's SCS-SF information PDF https://self-compassion.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/SCS-SF-information.pdf (sha256 4e0aacaae71a4f54a96e57118a2fde99ef242bc4b5462b85ddb7fdf76655f20a, fetched 2026-09-24). Scratch under itemtext/.cache/BPAQ_Christopher_2024_SCSS/.
note: ITEM AXIS, level-1, no inference: data/BPAQ_Christopher_2024.R selects starts_with('scssf') minus the recoded *r_b columns and scssf_selfComp_b and pivots with no rename, so the IRW code IS the deposit column name (derivation pattern 1). The deposit's Data Dictionary_RMH.xlsx labels measure 'scssf' variables q1..q12 as 'SCS-SF item #1'..'#12' with full wording (naming convention measure_variable_timepoint, b = Baseline); item_text is that wording, 12/12. DEVIATION: q2 reads 'understandin g' in the dictionary (a stray space) -- corrected to 'understanding'. CROSS-CHECK: all 12 dictionary items match Neff's SCS-SF form word for word; q8 carries a final period in the dictionary that the form lacks (kept, as in the dictionary); curly apostrophes kept as in the dictionary. STEP 3b: live items scssf_q1_b..q12_b, 12 items, resp 1-5, n=170 (paper: SCS-SF 12 items, 5-point, administered in both studies n=170) -- no instrument mismatch. STORAGE/POLARITY: items are stored RAW (the script drops the deposit's recoded q1r,q4r,q8r,q9r,q11r,q12r columns); reverse-scoring the form's negative items {1,4,8,9,11,12} on the live data gives total M=39.99 SD=7.42 (n=169 complete; one missing resp), against the paper's Table 1 SCS-SF M=39.99 SD=7.40 (n=170) and the deposit's scssf_selfComp_b (M 40.0, SD 7.4, n=170); the raw sum would be M=37.77 SD=5.37. Live q1 correlates +0.50..+0.57 with 4,8,9,11,12 and -0.12..-0.24 with 2,3,5,6,7,10, matching the form's keying. OPTION AXIS: neither the paper ('5-point Likert-type scale') nor the dictionary labels anchors; option_text is the form's endpoint labels 1=Almost never, 5=Almost always, with 2-4 left blank because the form labels only the endpoints. instructions = the form's sentence 'Please read each statement carefully before answering. Indicate how often you behave in the stated manner, using the following scale:' (canonical, not printed in the study's materials; the form's title 'HOW I TYPICALLY ACT TOWARDS MYSELF IN DIFFICULT TIMES' not shipped). Administered in English (US law-enforcement officers): no language or _translated columns. RIGHTS: register row 'Self-Compassion Scale Short Form (SCS-SF...)' verdict ship (2026-09-23, irw#2381 R03), applied not re-derived: 'Dr. Kristin Neff grants permission to use the Self-Compassion Scale Short Form (Raes et al., 2011) for any purpose whatsoever, including research, clinical work, teaching, etc.' -- the re-fetched PDF's sha256 matches the register's.

source_ref: Response data: OSF 3cgbt 'Conscientiousness and Internalizing Symptoms in Adolescence - Data' (public), '3. SAMPLE 3 Data.sav' https://osf.io/download/6616d64b943bee3e9bdfed54/ (452 rows, columns YIPS1..YIPS10, no variable or value labels). Wording: Renshaw, T. L. (2020). Youth Internalizing + Externalizing Problems Screeners (YIEPS): Measure and user guide, https://osf.io/download/ets7c/ (sha256 16500f8f439615ef2b237951b80f9fd7f2afa4de60d84faed64a8a2845d6312b), p.1 items 1-10 = Internalizing scale. Paper: Jovanovic (2026) J Individ Differ 47(1):32-39, doi 10.1027/1614-0001/a000455 (closed; Hogrefe 403).
note: mapping_basis=paper_order: data/jovanovic_2026_conscientiousness.py melts the Sample 3 .sav columns YIPS1..YIPS10 by name and lower-cases them (code IS the column name, core model s3 pattern 1), but the .sav has NO variable labels and NO value labels (checked with pyreadstat: all 11 YIPS* columns None), so what each column NUMBER means is inferred: yipsK = item K of the originator's form. The 'paper' here is the originator's form, not the study's paper. Renshaw's YIPS/YEPS hub (osf.io/63nzf wiki) says 'A free copy of the YIPS measure and user guide can be obtained via' osf.io/nz3a5, which serves exactly this YIEPS PDF, so items 1-10 of that PDF are the originator's distributed YIPS; supporting that the combined form preserves the standalone order, the standalone YEPS PDF (osf.io/download/wvgkz) lists its 10 items in the same order as YIEPS items 11-20. TEXT: text_source=translated_substitute. The study administered a Serbian version (Jovanovic & Renshaw, JPA 2023, 105(6), doi 10.1080/00223891.2023.2166518, paywalled). Recoverability checked in scope: the deposit (3 .sav files, OSF 3cgbt, no wiki, no components, no other files) holds no item wording in any script, and the paper is closed-access (OpenAlex oa_status=closed, Hogrefe 403), so no Serbian wording is recoverable; English originator wording ships in the base fields with _translated columns empty and language=Serbian. translation_source=official_instrument_english. Verbatim from the PDF: curly apostrophes (U+2019) kept in items 4, 7, 9; line wraps joined; 'Some-/times' column header joined as 'Sometimes'. Instructions are the YIEPS form's own ('...for how you felt in the past month.'); the Serbian administration's instructions and timeframe could not be checked. OPTIONS: 1 Almost Never, 2 Sometimes, 3 Often, 4 Almost Always per the PDF's 1-4 columns. Direction checked: YIPS item mean correlates +0.633 with the same respondents' SPANE negative-affect mean (n=452); every corrected item-total r positive (0.27-0.65), consistent with the guide's 'No reverse-scoring necessary'. All 10 items use all 4 levels. DATA NOTE: the deposit holds 8 fractional (imputed) YIPS cells (items 2,4,6,7,8) which the processing script drops, so those items have n 449-451 vs 452; live per-item resp multisets equal the deposit's integer cells 10/10. VERIFICATION: NO_ROUTE for item identity -- no per-item statistics are published for this sample, one 1-4 range, no subscales, no reverse items; a hypothetical anxiety/depression/somatic grouping via mapping_structure.R scored 4/9 (general factor dominates, not evidence either way). Post-hoc semantic read: highest means yips2 tired 2.44, yips6 moody 2.41; lowest yips9 worthless/lonely 1.63, yips7 panic 1.84, yips8 anhedonia 1.90 -- plausible, not a test. RIGHTS: applied existing instrument_rights_register.csv YIEPS row (verdict ship, Ben 2026-09-23, irw#2381 R05); re-fetched the PDF 2026-09-24, sha256 identical to the register's; quote present: 'The YIEPS is a “free cultural work,” licensed under a Creative Commons–Attribution 4.0 International license (CC BY 4.0)' and 'There is no cost for using the YIEPS and no need to obtain permission prior to use'. No register row written.
public_note: This study administered a Serbian translation of the YIPS; the item text shown is the originator's English wording in the originator's item order, and that yips1-yips10 follow that order is assumed from the column numbering rather than confirmed against the data.

source_ref: Atari et al. MFQ-2 Preprint R2 appendix, https://osf.io/download/br4zf/ (node osf.io/srtxn); data https://osf.io/2pkaw/ usData.rda
note: Item codes are the study's own column names in usData.rda (osf.io/2pkaw, CC BY 4.0; data/mft_validationandreplication.R takes the first 36 ^MFQ columns, no rename). The .rda carries no variable or value labels and the study's R scripts (dataAnalysis_US/UK, testRetest) contain no item wording, so there is no level-1 source. Zakharin & Bates (2023) PAID (CC BY) could not be read: sciencedirect and the Edinburgh repository copy (research.ed.ac.uk/files/365652333) both return a Cloudflare challenge; no wayback/Europe PMC copy. Wording, instructions and the 1-5 anchors are therefore from the originators' MFQ-2 appendix (Atari et al., 'MFQ-2 Preprint R2.pdf', osf.io/download/br4zf, node osf.io/srtxn, CC BY 4.0), with its scoring key Care=1,7,13,19,25,31; Equality=2,8,..; Proportionality=3,9,..; Loyalty=4,10,..; Authority=5,11,..; Purity=6,12,..,36. MFQ_<Foundation>k was mapped to the k-th item of that foundation in presentation order (e.g. MFQ_Pur2=item 12 chastity, MFQ_Pur6=item 36 virginity). This is consistent with the study's own script, which hard-codes Loyal1,2,4 as the country items and Loyal3,5,6 as community (appendix items 4,10,22 vs 16,28,34), and with its correlated residuals Pur2~Pur6, Prop1~Prop5, Auth1~Auth2, Auth3~Auth5, Care1~Care2, each a semantically paired item couple under this mapping. Wording variant: the originators' 'English Moral Foundations Questionnaire.docx' (osf.io/download/6bfe9, 2022-12) is identical to the appendix for 35/36 items but renders item 27 (MFQ_Prop5) as 'In a fair society, I want people who work harder than others to end up richer than others.' The appendix wording ('...those who work hard should live with higher standards of living.') was shipped; which version this study administered is not established because its paper was unreachable. Rights: applied instrument_rights_register.csv MFQ-2 row (verdict ship, 2026-09-23, originators' OSF node srtxn CC BY 4.0); not re-derived. Response rows: each item has 835 rows incl. 299 NA resp overall.
public_note: Item text is the MFQ-2 as published by its originators (Atari et al.); the study's own paper could not be checked, and for MFQ_Prop5 the originators also circulated an alternative wording ('In a fair society, I want people who work harder than others to end up richer than others'), so which version respondents saw is not confirmed.
